Second (Class-3, rank 2): 'Construction of division facts through equal sharing/ grouping and repeated subtraction)' (LCs: construct division facts through equal sharing and grouping; through repeated subtraction). Constructing division facts and constructing multiplication facts are inverse-operation fact-construction skills that meaningfully reinforce one another as fact families, which is exactly the operation-relationship coherence the shared Competency names, so this is substantive pair-specific coherence rather than generic repetition of the word 'facts'. It is not, however, a developmental dependency in the only permitted direction: Class-4 multiplication-fact construction is a different operation, not a deepening or extension of Class-3 division-fact construction, and the available evidence for that direction is limited to shared hierarchy, lexical overlap, and weak rank/page proximity. judgment.rationale: Both Content SFIs sit under Competency C-4.2 (selecting suitable units and tools for measuring attributes of objects) and CG-4, and each names a distinct measurable attribute with its own standard sub-unit and instrument: Class-4 'Measuring capacity of the vessels (millilitre) using measuring containers' and Class-5 'Measuring weight of the small objects (milligram) using weighing balance'. The shared substance is the coherent practice of choosing an appropriate standard unit and tool for fine-grained measurement, which is genuine conceptual/skill coherence. However, capacity-in-millilitres with measuring containers is not evidence that it supports success in weighing small objects in milligrams; the attributes, instruments and unit systems are parallel rather than cumulative, and the shared surface tokens ('measuring', 'using', 'of the') plus same-page/adjacent-rank proximity are not developmental evidence. The Class-4 to Class-5 rank gap alone therefore does not justify the permitted second_to_second_to_first buildsTowards direction, so the symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class-5 (rank 4) Content statements under the same measurement Curricular Goal CG-4 ('measure attributes such as distance, length, weight, area, capacity and time ... relating measure and number'), but sit under different competencies: C-4.3 (unit conversion within a measurement system, applied to everyday problems) and C-4.4 (strategies to estimate time). Their LCs show genuine skill coherence rather than mere wording overlap: 'convert units of length among metres, centimetres and millimetres' / 'convert units of weight among kilograms, grams and milligrams' alongside 'convert time between the 12-hour clock and the 24-hour clock' — the shared 'conversion' idea of re-expressing one measured quantity in an alternative unit/notation, reinforcing measurement sense across attributes. However, metric length/mass conversion is decimal and multiplicative while 12/24-hour clock conversion is a base-60/notation reading convention, so neither is evidenced as supporting success in the other; at equal Class-5 rank there is no substantive evidence for a developmental direction. Symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment. Both endpoints carry upstream merge/audit context and truncated source evidence (33 and 24 omitted items), so unseen source detail could refine but does not contradict this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both are Class-5 Content bullets (rank 4, equal) under the same Competency C-2.5 ('Identifies, describes and extends simple number patterns') and Curricular Goal CG-2. 'Palindrome numbers' (LCs: identify/describe/extend palindrome numbers) and 'Multiples and common multiples' (LCs: identify and find multiples of a given number; identify common multiples of two numbers) are distinct but coherent instances of the same competency work: recognising, describing and extending structured classes of numbers. judgment.rationale: Both are Content statements under the same competency C-3.1 (identifying and describing attributes of 2-D/3-D shapes with appropriate vocabulary). The Class-4 item covers properties of 2-D shapes (diagonals of square/rectangle/triangle; circle centre, radius, diameter; LCs 'Identify the centre/radius/diameter of a circle'), while the Class-5 item covers angles through clocks and time reading (LCs 'Identify angles formed by the hands of a clock', 'Read time on a clock'). There is genuine conceptual coherence — a clock face is a circle whose hands radiate from its centre, so circle-part vocabulary reinforces reasoning about angles at a centre — but the Class-4 content never addresses angles or angle measure, and the Class-5 content is framed around clocks/time rather than extending diagonals or circle parts. The evidence therefore supports substantive same-domain coherence rather than a justified developmental dependency, so relatesTo is preferred over the permitted first_to_second buildsTowards. Nomination signals (shared ancestors, same page, generic token overlap on 'a/identify/of/the/and') add no independent semantic weight. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each), and the shared ancestors carry merge/audit context and lack developmental coordinates, limiting confidence.

judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under the same Competency C-2.3 ('Visualises and recognizes relationships among operations...') and CG-2. The Class-3 item (rank 2) is about recognising the inverse relationship between multiplication and division through contexts and activity; the Class-5 item (rank 4) is about identifying patterns in number grids and multiplication tables. They share the multiplicative-structure domain (LC tags 'multiplication tables' vs 'multiplication', 'division', 'relationship') and are mutually reinforcing ways of exploring structure in multiplication, so there is genuine conceptual coherence. However, the evidence does not show that proficiency in recognising the multiplication–division inverse specifically supports success in detecting patterns in grids and tables: the Class-5 focus is pattern recognition in arrays/tables rather than operation inversion, and the only lexical link is the single token 'multiplication' (Jaccard ~0.06). That is insufficient to assert a developmental Class-3→Class-5 dependency, so the symmetric relation is the better-supported judgment. Both endpoints carry upstream merge/audit context (duplicate window extraction of one source bullet) and truncated source evidence; ancestors lack developmental coordinates and contribute context only.

The Class-3 item concerns weight (kilogram, more than/less than 1 kg, simple balance; LCs: compare and measure weight in kilograms with a simple balance), while the Class-4 item concerns length (centimetre using a scale; LC: measure length of objects in centimetre using a scale). They are parallel instantiations of the same measurement schema — choosing a standard unit and an appropriate tool to quantify an attribute of objects — which is substantive complementary coherence beyond the shared parent and the generic shared tokens ("measure", "objects", "using"). However, the attributes, units, and instruments differ entirely, so proficiency in weighing with a balance does not specifically support success in measuring length with a scale; the one-class rank gap alone is not developmental evidence, so buildsTowards is not warranted. This is complementary reinforcement rather than development: pattern-play under the representation-oriented competency C-2.1 is not a deepening, extension, or increased-complexity version of the specific multiplication skill under C-2.3, and nothing in the bounded Content, Competency, or LC text states that pattern identification depends on multiplication-fact proficiency. judgment.rationale: First (Class-4, rank 3, under Competency C-2.3 'applies the four basic operations... to solve real-life problems') is 'Addition and subtraction up to 10000 in contexts; in abstract form', with LCs on adding and subtracting numbers up to 10000. Second (Class-5, rank 4, under Competency C-2.1 'Represents numbers using the place-value system... reads the number names') is 'Numbers and number names beyond 10000 based on the place value', with LCs on representing numbers beyond 10000 by place value and reading their number names. The pair shares the CG-2 whole-number goal and the same 10000 number range, so there is genuine conceptual coherence: operating fluently within 10000 reinforces the place-value structure that the Class-5 content extends beyond 10000. However, the two sit under different competencies addressing different strands (computation with operations vs. numeration/representation and number names), and the Class-5 target depends primarily on prior place-value/numeration content rather than on addition/subtraction proficiency, so the evidence does not support asserting a developmental dependency from first to second. Nomination signals (shared ancestor CG-2, one shared LC token '10000', weak rank and page proximity) are corroborative context only, not dependency evidence. Second SFI (Class-3, rank 2, Competency C-2.3 on relationships among operations) is 'Construction of division facts through equal sharing/ grouping and repeated subtraction' with LCs on constructing division facts via equal sharing/grouping and via repeated subtraction. judgment.rationale: Both are Class-4 Content bullets in the same C-2.5 number-patterns competency row (rank 3 each). The first ('Order of numbers in multiplication'; LC: recognise that changing the order of numbers in multiplication does not change the product) addresses commutativity, while the second ('Patterns in multiplication (5x10, 5x100, 5x1000)'; LC: identify and extend patterns when multiplying by 10, 100 and 1000) addresses place-value/powers-of-ten regularities. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Content SFIs under Competency C-2.3 ('applies the four basic operations on numbers') and Curricular Goal CG-2 (whole-number fluency, place value). The first (Class-4, rank 3) covers multi-digit multiplication procedures (2-digit x 1-digit, 2-digit x 2-digit, 3-digit x 1-digit; LCs match exactly these). The second (Class-5, rank 4) covers understanding powers of 10 seen so far and all four operations on them (LCs: understand, add, subtract, multiply, divide powers of 10). This is substantive complementary coherence: multiplicative reasoning about powers of 10 is the place-value structure that multi-digit multiplication algorithms exploit, and both are whole-number operation content under the same competency, so the two mutually reinforce. It is not, however, a developmental extension of the first skill: the Class-5 statement narrows the number class to powers of 10 while broadening across four operations rather than deepening multi-digit multiplication, and the remaining nomination signals (shared ancestors, one-rank gap, jaccard 0.06 LC overlap on 'multiplication'/'multiply', shared SFI token only 'of', weak rank and page proximity) are insufficient to establish that proficiency in the first supports success in the second. The LC sets overlap substantively on 'solve ... problems using addition/subtraction', giving genuine reinforcement of the same application-problem skill across two different contexts (measurement quantities vs. money amounts).
